title: Power Apps: prompt columns can store multiple lines of text output
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, credit consumption and general prompt-column controls are supported. Microsoft still does not document the multi-line option's default or length limit. The environment control's navigation is supported, but the briefing should acknowledge that two cited Learn pages place its toggle under different headings.

claims.quote: Prompt columns can now store multilple lines of text as prompt output

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Updating one or more referenced input columns triggers prompt-column execution, subject to its controls and filters.
claims.quote: A prompt executes when you create a record or update one or more of the columns that the prompt references. If none of the referenced columns change, the prompt doesn't run and no extra credits are consumed.

claims.claim: Learn states that on-demand prompt-column execution is not currently supported.

claims.claim: Insufficient permission on an input column is a documented cause of prompt-column generation failure.
claims.quote: The user doesn't have sufficient permissions on one or more input columns referenced in the prompt column definition.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls: monitoring
claims.claim: Power Automate > Automation center > AI Builder activity opens the prompt-column credit consumption report.
claims.quote: Sign in to Power Automate. On the left navigation pane, select Automation center, and then select AI Builder activity.

claims.claim: The report's Estimated consumption column shows credits consumed by each prompt execution.
claims.quote: Review the Estimated consumption column to see the credits consumed by each prompt execution.

claims.claim: Prompt-column filter conditions reduce unnecessary executions and help optimise credit consumption.
claims.quote: During record creation or update, the prompt column evaluates the filter first and then executes the prompt for eligible records. This approach reduces unnecessary executions and helps optimize Copilot credit consumption.

claims.claim: Prompt-run cost depends on input tokens, output tokens and model version.
claims.quote: The combination of input tokens, output tokens, and the model version allows you to compute the cost of your prompt run.

claims.claim: Prompt runs consume the environment's available AI credit capacity.
claims.quote: Once an environment has Copilot Credits available, it can run the AI Builder features in all contexts. If an environment only has AI Builder credits available, it can only run AI Builder features in Power Apps and Power Automate.

claims.claim: Prompt-column prerequisites require the environment's Copilot feature to be on.
claims.quote: Copilot and AI Prompts features turned On in the Features area for the environment settings.

claims.claim: The environment AI prompts feature controls prompt-column execution.
claims.quote: Common scenarios where the prompt doesn't execute, no error is surfaced, and execution is skipped: AI Prompt feature is disabled.

claims.claim: A table can contain up to five prompt columns.
claims.quote: You can create up to five prompt columns per table.

claims.claim: Block unmanaged customizations must be disabled to create or edit prompt columns.

claims.fix: Append to controls[0].note: 'Administer AI Builder places this toggle under AI Builder; Manage feature settings lists it under AI prompts (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/settings-features#ai-prompts).' Manage feature settings also supports the initial Manage > Environments steps; retain the existing path.

claims.claim: PATCH /api/data/v9.2/organizations(<organizationid>) updates the organization containing the AI prompts setting.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations. Primary key: organizationid. Operations supported: GETPATCH.

claims.claim: The PATCH request body sets the Boolean aipromptsenabled property to enable or disable AI prompts.
claims.quote: aipromptsenabled | Edm.Boolean | Indicates whether AI Prompts feature is enabled. Display name: Enable AI Prompts.

claims.claim: An AI prompts environment group rule can govern AI prompts availability for the group's environments.
claims.quote: If your environment is part of an environment group, you can also govern AI prompts feature availability through the AI prompts environment group rule.

claims.claim: Publishing the AI prompts group rule locks the setting at environment level.
claims.quote: If an environment group rule governing AI prompts is published, it locks the AI prompts setting at the environment-level, preventing any system administrator of those individual environments from editing the setting.

claims.claim: To change a locked AI prompts setting, administrators must modify the corresponding environment group rule.
claims.quote: To change the setting, admins must modify the corresponding rule in the environment group that includes the environment.

claims.quote: Select Tables on the left navigation pane. Open the table, select Columns, and then open the column that is of data type Prompt where you want to disable AI generation. On the Edit column pane, clear the Allow prompt column execution checkbox

claims.claim: Allow prompt column execution is enabled by default for a prompt column.
claims.quote: By default, the Allow prompt column execution setting is enabled.

claims.claim: Disabling Allow prompt column execution stops AI analysis for that individual prompt column.
claims.quote: When disabled, AI analysis isn't performed for the prompt column.

claims.claim: Learn says both tenant-level and column-level settings must be enabled for prompts to execute.
claims.quote: For prompts to be executed, both tenant level and column level settings need to be enabled.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second row; Open questions
claims.claim: No API or command is documented for the Allow prompt column execution setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse Allow prompt column execution API attribute entity reference msdyn aiconfiguration disable execution PowerShell pac. Read prompt-column, specialized-columns, msdyn_aiconfiguration reference and pac copilot excerpts; no operation/property for this setting.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated what multi-line output does on arrival, so its default state is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt columns" "multi-line" "default" "settings"; Dataverse prompt columns multiple lines text output length limit default existing columns rollout licensing. Read roadmap record, prompt-column, administer and settings-features; no multi-line arrival default.

claims.claim: No new admin switch specific to multi-line prompt output is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt columns" "multi-line" licensing rollout existing admin switch; "prompt columns" "multi-line" "default" "settings". Read prompt-column, administer, settings-features and organization reference; found general controls, not a multi-line switch.

claims.claim: The prompt-columns Learn page does not describe multi-line output as of this check.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt columns" "multiple lines" "output". Read the full https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/prompt-column page; it describes prompts, asynchronous execution, filters, backfill and execution controls, but not multi-line output.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented how multi-line prompt output is chosen.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt columns" "multiple lines" "output"; "prompt columns" "multi-line" "default" "settings". Read prompt-column and relevant search excerpts; no selection procedure for multi-line output.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: No source states whether the multi-line output change alters existing prompt columns.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt columns" "multi-line" licensing rollout existing admin switch. Read roadmap record and prompt-column; the latter describes existing definitions changing for asynchronous execution, but does not connect that upgrade to multi-line output.

claims.claim: A stored multi-line prompt-output length limit is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt column" "output" "maximum" "length"; Dataverse prompt columns multiple lines text output length limit default existing columns rollout licensing. Read prompt-column, specialized-columns and text-column type excerpts; no limit tied to this multi-line feature.

claims.claim: No licensing provision specific to multi-line output is published beyond general prompt consumption licensing.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt columns" "multi-line" licensing rollout existing admin switch. Read prompt-column, prompts-overview, administer-licensing and licensing-prompt-tokens; general prompt credits and token rates are published, but no separate multi-line licensing provision.

claims.claim: Rollout mechanics specific to multi-line prompt-column output are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt columns" "multi-line" licensing rollout existing admin switch. Read roadmap record and prompt-column; November CY2026 is a roadmap target, and Learn's regional upgrade notes concern asynchronous execution/backfill, not multi-line output.

claims.claim: Learn does not tie either listed execution control specifically to multi-line output; both are general prompt-column controls.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt columns" "multi-line" "default" "settings". Read prompt-column, administer, settings-features and organization reference; their controls govern AI prompts or column execution without mentioning multi-line output.

claims.claim: The roadmap description mentions no new connector, identity or permission.
claims.quote: Prompt columns can now store multilple lines of text as prompt output, enabling longer and detailed AI-generated insights to be stored in your tables.

claims.claim: The prompt designer's Test option can test real table records before the prompt is saved.
claims.quote: When you create a prompt column, you can test the prompt against real data in your table before you save it. In the prompt designer, select Test.

claims.claim: The prompt-column Status and Details columns can be added to the table view to expose execution failures.
claims.quote: Search and select the columns named: (columnName) _PromptColumnStatus; (columnName)_PromptColumnDetails. Select Save. Select Edit to the right of the list to open the columns list with records in a separate view.
